summary: Persistent remote code execution via IPNS-fetched Fernet-encrypted Python modules
details: scrapetools2/downloader.py fetches a tar.gz from an author-controlled IPNS pointer (k51qzi5uqu5dmh5178x8jzdkz8u3k3qona4zrwlvdr6865it3901l1oe8emjwc) through gateways eu.orbitor.dev, dget.top, and ipfs.filebase.io, decrypts the archive contents using Fernet keys shipped in scrapetools2/versions, writes them to modules/*.py, then compiles and exec's each module. browser_pool.DBConsumer.updater() spawns a daemon thread that repeats this fetch-decrypt-exec cycle every 60 seconds, providing a persistent pull channel for arbitrary code delivery. The payload is additionally obfuscated: scrapetools2/updates ships a z85-encoded Fernet ciphertext and scrapetools2/versions ships the corresponding z85-encoded Fernet key, defeating source review of what will be executed. Because IPNS is a mutable pointer controlled by the publisher, the code executed on installer hosts can be changed at any time after publication with no version bump and no integrity check available to the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
